 SES Hosts Webinar on Landfill Diversion for Organic Waste and Food Recall Events
 The Nov. 12 webinar will be led by Simplified Environmental Solutions Chief Revenue Officer Jeff Hinds and is designed for food and beverage manufacturers, plant managers and sustainability leaders.
 Courtesy Simplified Environmental Solutions 
 Posted by 
 Jacqueline Mitchell, Editor, QA 
 Published November 12, 2026 
 Listen to article 
 / 
 CHESTERFIELD, Mo. – Simplified Environmental Solutions (SES) will host a free live webinar, "Zero Waste Webinar: Tackling Organic Waste & Recalled Foods," on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 2 p.m. CT. The session will be led by SES Chief Revenue Officer Jeff Hinds and is designed for food and beverage manufacturers, plant managers and sustainability leaders.
 Every year, over 60 million tons of food are wasted and landfilled in the US, according to the EPA. That waste creates methane emissions, leachate problems, odors, and contamination, and wastes valuable resources, said SES. Hinds will discuss how food and beverage manufacturers can keep that waste out of landfills and put those resources back to productive use. He will also explain why a product recall, often treated as a disposal problem, is an opportunity to recover value and strengthen a company's sustainability record.
 "I spent 30 years on the production side of the food industry, and I know how much good product and packaging ends up landfills simply because no one had a better plan," said Hinds. "A recall event or an off-spec run doesn't have to be a total loss. With the right process, everything in that waste stream can be recovered and reused, and I look forward to showing companies how to make that happen."
 The webinar will cover:
 What happens to food waste after it leaves a production facility, and how to control it
 How food waste de-packaging and reclamation keep packaged product and organics out of the landfill
 How to protect brand and material resources during a recall event
 How to build and track a Zero Waste to Landfill program that advances sustainability goals and meets diversion mandates
